newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta share prices end 1.06 pct lower on Telkom.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta share prices end 1.06 pct lower on Telkom.

text.p: A sell-off in blue chip Telkom as well as cigarette makers Gudang Garam and Sampoerna pushed down the Jakarta shares index down 1.06 at the close on Friday, brokers said.

Telkom, Gudang Garam and Sampoerna are among the heaviest weighted stocks on the Jakarta Composite Index which dropped 7.03 points, or 1.06 percent, to 656.11 points after hitting an intra-day low of 653.98 points during afternoon trading.
In the broad market sentiment, losers led gainers by 71 to 43, with 57 counters unchanged.
Total turnover was 471.8 billion rupiah on a volume of 185.9 million shares. The index was down about 1.6 percent, or 10.72 points, on the week.
Sustained selling in blue chips led by Telkom had dampened overall market sentiment, especially towards big-capitalised stocks, brokers said.

They said further selling in heavyweight Telkom was partly triggered by further cross-trading towards the close of the afternoon session. "It once again sparked speculation on who the cross-trading buyers were," a local broker said.
It was cross-traded at 3,700 rupiah on a turnover of 40.8 million shares. On the regular board, Telkom was off 100 rupiah at 3,625 rupiah on 12.1 million shares traded.

But some analysts and brokers believed the Telkom fall was also linked to the possible emergence of a competitor which analysts said was clouding Telkom's outlook despite its better-than-expected 1.5 trillion rupiah net profit for 1996.
Market sentiment was also hit by concern that the U.S. Federal Reserve might raise interest rates at next Tuesday's meeting.
"I believe the market will rebound after the U.S. Federal Reserve announces the results of its meeting next week," a broker with a foreign firm said.

Analysts and brokers said a new government regulation authorising the customs and excise department to set the retail prices of cigarettes from April 1 had sparked concern over the possible impact on the bottom-lines of Gudang Garam and Sampoerna.
The ruling states that cigarette producers and importers can now only propose the retail prices for their products.

Analysts said the aim of the regulation seemed unclear, adding that it lacked details and they needed time to study the ruling, which put a negative sentiment on cigarette firms listed on the Jakarta exchange.
Sampoerna was off 300 rupiah to 11,050 rupiah on a volume of 589,500 shares, while Gudang Garam was down 275 rupiah to 10,075 rupiah on 807,000 shares.

"I don't know what impact this ruling will have on retail prices and on the bottom-lines of cigarette companies," one analyst with a Singapore-based firm said. "But my initial feeling is that the move will have some impact on earnings of cigarette companies."
Secondary transportation company Mitra Rajasa was the most active stock with about 15 million shares changing hands, rising 19.05 percent to 1,875 rupiah.

"I heard they are going to link-up with foreign partners," said a broker with a Malaysian firm, adding that he had also heard that the firm had obtained a significant contract order from a big company which would effect its 1997 earnings.
Company officials were not immediately available for comment.
